title: fix(app-shell,plugin-designer): the designer's nav surfaces show a label-less entry's inherited label, the way the console draws it (objectui#11196)
body:
Part of #11196
Clause-②: no

Most of objectui#11196: every designer surface this claim covers, including the Studio rail rows (after PR objectui#11202 reached `main`; this branch merges it). Two sites from the card's own `sweep.SEAM` list are outside this claim's file surface and are not touched (see Remainder), so this PR does not close the card.

## What changed

A nav entry with no `label` inherits its target's CURRENT label at render time. The console already draws it that way (sidebar, `nav:menu`, command palette, search, since PR objectui#11186). The designer surfaces read the raw label instead. Every surface below now asks the runtime's own rule, `resolveNavItemLabel` from `@object-ui/layout`. None keeps a second ladder, and `packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` is not edited.

| surface | before, for a label-less entry | now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `AppPreview` list (`normalizeNav`) and its landing line | `(unnamed)` | inherited text |
| `AppNavCanvas` card (`navLabel`) | positional `Item N` | inherited text; the inline rename shows it as the input's placeholder |
| `AppNavInspector` title | `label ?? title ?? name`, else the positional selection id | inherited text |
| `AppNavInspector` Label field | empty value, no hint; a map label showed `[object Object]` | value = authored label only; placeholder = inherited text |
| `nav-selection.ts` `findNavPositionById` | `label ?? title ?? name` | authored plain-string `label` only; the inspector names the entry from the entry itself |
| Studio Interfaces rail, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` `NavTree` rows | leaf: the target's internal name; group heading: blank | inherited text; the internal identity stays on the tooltip |
| plugin-designer `NavigationDesigner` row and its live preview | blank | the rule's own answer: the machine-name rung, because it is handed no metadata |
| plugin-designer `AppCreationWizard`'s Navigation step | blank | each object's label, from the wizard's own object list (a host `NavTargetLabelResolver` handed to the rule) |

- **One rule, extended rather than forked.** `previews/navItemLabel.ts` gains `navEntryLabelText` and `inheritedNavEntryText`. They call `resolveNavItemLabel`: an authored label reads through the existing `navItemLabelText` in the designer locale, and an absent one goes to the runtime's ladder. Carrier rider (`5909012131`): the module docblock now says `navItemLabelText` reads any `I18nLabel` (app and action labels too). The rename is not done, because it would touch `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `ObjectActionsPanel.tsx`, which are outside this claim.
- **Resolver.** The app-shell surfaces pass the console's own `useNavTargetLabel`. Measured: it resolves in the console's i18next language, and the designer locale (`useMetadataLocale`) is that same language collapsed to `en-US` / `zh-CN`. So a label-less entry reads in the designer exactly as the console draws it. A designer-locale twin would have needed either a second metadata resolver or an edit to `useNavTargetLabel.ts`, which is outside this claim. Limit: in a session of one of the eight other shipped locales, inherited text follows the console language, while the designer resolves an authored map label in English.
- **Fallback.** Same as the runtime's: the target's machine name (`objectName`, `dashboardName`, `pageName`, ...), else the entry's `id`. A target the host cannot read (a draft, an unsaved page, no metadata loaded) falls to the machine name, as it does in the console before its metadata loads. `engine.appPreview.unnamed` and the positional `engine.appNav.item` row stay only for what the rule names nothing: a separator, a label that is present but resolves to nothing (an empty map), and an entry with no target and no `id`. No i18n string is added or removed.
- **Editing keeps inheritance.** On the canvas and in the inspector, inherited text is a placeholder, never a stored value, so an untouched entry stays label-less. Typing writes an author label; a locale map changes only the designer locale's entry, through the existing `renamedLabel`. Emptying the inspector field restores inheritance: the new `clearedLabel` (the inverse of `renamedLabel`) answers what is left, and when nothing is left the `label` key is removed, never written as `''`.
- **plugin-designer.** It now depends on `@object-ui/layout`. There is no cycle: layout depends on components, core, react and types, and none of them depends on plugin-designer. Bundle: plugin-designer's vite build externalizes every bare specifier. Measured on the built `dist/index.js`: one `import ... from "@object-ui/layout"` and 0 inlined definitions of the ladder. For a consumer, layout is side-effectful and brings `@dnd-kit`, but the console already ships it. The Navigation Designer is handed bare items and no metadata, so it shows the rule's machine-name rung. The app wizard's Navigation step hands the rule a host resolver built from its own object list, so a label-less object entry shows the object's label there. For pages (what the console's navigation sync writes) that is exactly what the console shows. A label-less dashboard shows `dashboardName` where the console shows its label. The seat has the options for that.

## Remainder (not in this PR)

- **`resolveSurface`'s `Surface.label`** (`navSurface.ts`). It is unchanged: it still carries `''` for a label-less entry. Its readers are the canvas caption, the breadcrumb and the copilot chip, all in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` outside the `NavTree` rows this claim allows. The chip's `type · name` fallback for an unlabelled leaf is pinned by `StudioDesignSurface.aiChipLabel.test.tsx` (objectui#8219 item 3). Making them inherit is a ruling for the seat, not a line change.
- **`StudioNavItemInspector`** (in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`). Its label reads are in the card's `sweep.SEAM` list, but outside this claim's file surface ("`NavTree` rows only"). Two gaps remain there. Clearing its Label field writes `''` through `renamedLabel`. Picking an object for a label-less entry stores the object's label, where the entry would otherwise keep inheriting it.

- **`AppNavCanvas`'s `addItem` birth label.** A new entry is born with the localized "New item" label, and `AppNavInspector`'s object picker keeps it, so the entry never inherits.

The seat answered the dev's open questions (`5914452475` gives the review's readings): `resolveSurface` inherits (A, with the objectui#8219 chip pin re-judged); `StudioNavItemInspector` follows `AppNavInspector`'s shape (A); `addItem` births a label-less entry (A, with the objectui#11189 autosave pins re-judged). All three are this card's next slice, after PR objectui#11225 lands, because they share its `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` hunks. `NavigationDesigner` stays on the machine-name rung until a host with metadata appears.

## Acceptance notes

- `AppNavInspector`'s `ensureNavId` builds an id from `String(node.objectName ?? node.label ?? 'item')`. For an entry with no `id` and no `objectName` whose label is a locale map, that reads `[object Object]` and would yield `nav_object_object`. This is a read-only inference, not reproduced; the spec requires every nav entry to carry an `id`. Not in scope here.
- The designer-locale limit above: in a session of a locale other than en / zh, inherited text follows the console language, while the designer resolves authored map labels in English.

objectui#11197 landed as PR objectui#11207 (`e6bc087a3`), which also edited `AppPreview.tsx`, `AppNavCanvas.tsx` and `NavigationDesigner.tsx`. This branch merged `main` at `6e8f1d83f`:
- one textual conflict, in the `AppPreview.tsx` imports, where both lines are kept;
- one semantic clash: objectui#11197's `AppPreview.docEntry-11197` pin now finds a label-less `doc` entry's text twice (its target, and its inherited label), so its two assertions use `getAllByText`. The entry is still kept, badged `doc`, with its target shown.

The parity pin gains three label-less `doc` entries (with a page, with only a book, with neither). For each, the designer answers exactly what the runtime answers: the page, else the book, else the `id`.
